name: How Fencing Contractors in Los Angeles County Manage Mid-Project Changes

mainEntity.name: How do Los Angeles County fencing contractors usually handle mid-project design changes, and what should I have in writing?
mainEntity.text: How do Los Angeles County fencing contractors usually handle mid-project design changes, and what should I have in writing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fence projects often evolve once old structures are removed or homeowners see the new layout taking shape. To avoid disputes in Los Angeles County, ask your fencing contractor how they handle mid-project design changes before work starts. They should use a written change-order process that describes the new work, additional materials, updated labor, and any schedule impact. Request that all changes affecting cost or scope be documented and signed by you before the crew proceeds, rather than agreed to verbally on-site. Clarify how design tweaks—such as changing fence height, adding lattice, upgrading hardware, or extending the project area—will be priced and whether they require extra deposits. Ask whether change orders are billed at the same rate as the original contract or at a different hourly or unit rate. Make sure your contract states that the original scope remains unchanged unless modified by written change orders, protecting both parties from misunderstandings. Establishing this process up front keeps your project flexible while maintaining clear expectations for cost and schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask contractors to explain their change-order process, including how design changes are documented, priced, and approved before work continues. Your contract should require written change orders for any added cost or scope changes during the fence project.
